chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, who said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman narrated from Musa al-Marwazi, from Abu al-Hasan (the first Imam, peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Four [acts] corrupt the heart and sprout hypocrisy in the heart as water sprouts trees: listening to vain talk, and coarse speech, and going to the door of the ruler, and seeking hunting.
ai.seo_question: What are the four acts that corrupt the heart and develop hypocrisy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate how external sensory inputs and social behaviors gradually cultivate *nifaq* (hypocrisy) within the heart. The comparison to water nurturing trees emphasizes the organic and inevitable growth of these spiritual defects when left unchecked. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on purifying the heart (*tazkiyat al-qalb*) by guarding against both verbal excesses and the political compromises of frequenting royal courts.
